description:
## Goal

Make JIT/AOT compilation incremental below the whole-root NativeProgram boundary: compile only new or changed native bodies and relink the exact affected root artifact.

## Current defect

Each run/build request constructs a fresh backend and defines every function in the NativeProgram. The 00420 trace records 943 function-definition spans and the native backend compile span is about 3.19 seconds. Whole-root dense `FnId` assignment and fresh backend lifetime prevent reuse even when most bodies are unchanged.

## Strategy

1. Give native bodies stable semantic product identities independent of root-relative dense order.
2. Publish one immutable native-body product per executable/wrapper plus a root link/entry product.
3. Persist compiled body generations in the compiler-owned backend cache.
4. Invalidate only bodies whose native input products move; relink only when membership, symbol, or relocation dependencies move.
5. Define eviction and target/configuration identity explicitly; never reuse across incompatible codegen settings.
6. Delete whole-program body walking and fresh-backend recompilation paths once all front doors use the keyed cache.

## Signal

- Same compiler/root twice: zero body lowering and zero function compilation.
- Unreachable edit: zero native work.
- Reached leaf edit: only the exact body and relocation/link dependents compile.
- Equal reproduction preserves generations and performs no work.
- JIT and AOT output, ABI, symbols, debug behavior, and runtime results remain identical.
- Causal generation/work counts, not wall-clock thresholds, are the acceptance oracle.
- Full tests, fixture matrix, cross-process determinism, formatting, and strict clippy pass.
title: Reuse native code generation by changed function generation
